traits.name: Size
traits.text: Aegyls are Medium creatures and have no bonuses or penalties due to their size.

traits.name: Type
traits.text: Aegyls are Humanoid creatures with the aegyl subtype.

traits.name: Base Speed
traits.text: Aegyls have a base speed of 30 feet on land. They also have a fly speed of 40 feet (poor), an aegyl’s wing span is typically 12 feet, and cannot fly in an area that does not allow them to fully extend their wings.

traits.name: Languages
traits.text: Aegyls begin play speaking Common and Aegyllan. Aegyl with high Intelligence scores can choose from the following: Draconic, Dwarven, Elvaan, Galkan, Giant, Goblin, and Orc. See the Linguistics skill page for more information about these languages.

traits.name: Elemental Resistance
traits.text: Aegyls have wind and lightning elemental resistance 5.

traits.name: Eternal Hope
traits.text: Aegyls gain a +2 racial bonus on saving throws against fear and despair effects. Also, once per day, after a natural roll of 1 on a d20 roll, aegyls may reroll and use the second result.

traits.name: Illusion Resistance
traits.text: Aegyls gain a +2 racial bonus on saving throws against illusion spells or effects.

traits.name: Keen Senses
traits.text: Aegyls receive a +2 racial bonus on Perception checks.

traits.name: Low-Light Vision
traits.text: An aegyl can see twice as far as a hume in starlight, moonlight, torchlight, and similar conditions of poor illumination. He retains the ability to distinguish color and detail under these conditions.

traits.name: Emotionless
traits.text: Aegyls are cold and aloof. They do not like dealing with other races other than their own. They receive a –2 penalty on Diplomacy checks when dealing with other races.

traits.name: Size
traits.text: Al Bheds are Medium creatures and thus receive no bonuses or penalties due to their size.

traits.name: Type
traits.text: Al Bheds are Humanoid creatures with the al bhed subtype.

traits.name: Base Speed
traits.text: Al Bheds have a base speed of 30 feet.

traits.name: Languages
traits.text: Al Bheds begin play speaking Common and Albhedian. Al Bheds with high Intelligence scores can choose from the following: Goblin, Loporrit, Moogle, PuPon, and Yagudo. See the Linguistics skill page for more information about these languages.

traits.name: Desert Nomad
traits.text: Al Bheds thrive in the deepest deserts, forever roaming across burned and parched lands. They gain a +4 racial bonus on Constitution checks and Fortitude saves to avoid fatigue, exhaustion, or ill effects from running, forced marches, starvation, thirst, or hot or cold environments.

traits.name: Trap Knowledge
traits.text: Al Bheds know the inner mechanical workings of most traps. They gain +2 racial bonus on all saving throws versus mechanical traps.

traits.name: Fixer-Upper
traits.text: Al Bheds gain the Repair skill as a class skill regardless of class. In addition, they never take penalties for not having a toolkit while using the Repair skill. Furthermore, they only take 30 minutes to use the Repair skill to repair damage done to a construct.

traits.name: Mechanical Genius
traits.text: At first level, Al Bheds gain an additional skill rank and a +2 racial bonus to skill rolls which they must apply to one of the following: Knowledge (engineering), Profession (engineering), Craft (any), Disable Device, or Use Magical Device. These skills are always considered class skills for an al bhed.

traits.name: Skill Training
traits.text: Al Bheds treat Drive and Pilot as class skills.

traits.name: Technologist
traits.text: Al Bheds are intuitive and have an innate understanding of technology, gaining Technologist as a bonus feat.

traits.name: Weapon Familiarity
traits.text: Al Bheds are proficient with Simple Firearms.

traits.name: Size
traits.text: Auri are Medium creatures and thus receive no bonuses or penalties due to their size.

traits.name: Type
traits.text: Auri are Humanoid creatures with the Au ra subtype.

traits.name: Base Speed
traits.text: Auri have a base speed of 30 feet.

traits.name: Languages
traits.text: Auri begin play speaking Common and Draconic. Auri with high Intelligence scores can choose from the following: Elvaan, Galkan, Goblin, Kojin, Matanga, and Orc. See the Linguistics skill page for more information about these languages.

traits.name: Elemental Resistance
traits.text: Auri have ice resistance 5, lightning resistance 5, and fire resistance 5.

traits.name: Scales
traits.text: Auri’s patches of scales along their body grant them a +1 natural armor bonus to their Armor Class.

traits.name: Fearless
traits.text: Auri get a +2 racial bonus on all saving throws against fear.

traits.name: Imposing Figure
traits.text: Xaela are intimidating without trying due their draconic features, large bodies, and cold glowing gazes. They gain a +2 racial bonus to Intimidate checks. (Skill Bonus1)

traits.name: Survivalist
traits.text: All auri gain a +2 racial bonus on all Survival checks. (Skill Bonus)

traits.name: Ferocity
traits.text: Once per day, when au ras are brought below 0 hit points but not killed, they can fight on for 1 more round as if disabled. At the end of their next turn, unless brought to above 0 hit points, they immediately fall unconscious and begin dying. (This acts as Orc Ferocity)

traits.name: Darkvision
traits.text: All auri can see perfectly in the dark up to 60 feet.

traits.name: Size
traits.text: Bangaa are Medium creatures, and have no bonuses or penalties due to their size.

traits.name: Type
traits.text: Bangaa are Humanoid creatures with the reptilian subtype.

traits.name: Base Speed
traits.text: Bangaa have a base speed of 30 feet on land.

traits.name: Languages
traits.text: Bangaa begin play speaking Common and Banganese. Bangaa with high Intelligence can choose bonus languages from the following: Draconic, Giant, Ignan, Numish, Seeq, Terran.

traits.name: Desert Delver
traits.text: Bangaa have adapted to the extremes of cold and heat that can suddenly occur in both the harsh deserts and the mountain tunnels around their caravan routes. Bangaa gain a +4 racial bonus on Constitution checks and Fortitude saves to avoid fatigue, exhaustion, and other ill effects from running, forced marches, starvation, thirst, and hot or cold environments, and treat the temperature as 20 degrees cooler or warmer when determining the effects of extreme heat or extreme cold environments. This counts as the Endurance feat for qualifying for feats, but will otherwise stack with the feat.

traits.name: Elemental Resistance
traits.text: Due to their life in the sands and scaly exteriors, the bangaa have a higher resilience to the elements. Bangaa gain resistance 5 against fire and ice.

traits.name: Stability
traits.text: Bangaa receive a +4 racial bonus to their Combat Maneuver Defense when resisting a bull rush or trip attempt while standing on the ground.

traits.name: Thick-skinned
traits.text: A bangaa’s tough and scaly hide grants a +1 bonus to natural armor.

traits.name: Keen Senses
traits.text: Bangaa receive a +2 racial bonus on Perception checks.

traits.name: Well-Balanced
traits.text: Bangaa receive a +2 racial bonus on Acrobatics checks.

traits.name: Bite
traits.text: Bangaa gain a natural bite attack, dealing 1d3 points of damage. The bite is a primary attack, or a secondary attack if the bangaa is wielding manufactured weapons.

traits.name: Deft Pugilist
traits.text: Bangaa learn from an early age their agility is their greatest asset, train their bodies to capitalize. Bangaa are always considered armed and do not provoke an attack of opportunity for making an unarmed attack.

traits.name: Low-Light Vision
traits.text: Bangaa have low-light vision allowing them to see twice as far as humes in dim light.

traits.name: Size
traits.text: Beastkins are Medium creatures and have no bonuses or penalties due to their size.

traits.name: Type
traits.text: Beastkins are Humanoid creatures with the beastkin subtype.

traits.name: Base Speed
traits.text: Beastkins have a base speed of 30 feet.

traits.name: Languages
traits.text: Beastkins begin play speaking Common and Beastmen. Beastkin with high Intelligence scores can choose from the following: Draconic, Dwarven, Elvaan, Galkan, Giant, Goblin, and Orc. See the Linguistics skill page for more information about these languages.

traits.name: Beastkin Immunities
traits.text: Beastkins are immune to magic sleep effects and gain a +2 racial saving throw bonus against enfeebling spells and effects.

traits.name: Fearless
traits.text: Beastkins gain a +2 racial bonus on all saving throws against fear effects.

traits.name: Natural Armor
traits.text: Beastkins have a +1 natural armor bonus.

traits.name: Fleet-Footed
traits.text: Beastkins receive Run as a bonus feat and a +2 racial bonus on initiative checks.

traits.name: Hunter
traits.text: Beastkins always count Stealth and Survival as class skills.

traits.name: Keen Senses
traits.text: Beastkins receive a +2 racial bonus on Perception checks.

traits.name: Sprinter
traits.text: Beastkins gain a 10-foot racial bonus to their speed when using the charge, run, or withdraw actions.

traits.name: Darkvision
traits.text: Beastkins can see perfectly in the dark up to 60 feet.

traits.name: Low-Light Vision
traits.text: Beastkins have low-light vision allowing them to see twice as far as humes in dim light.

traits.name: Size
traits.text: Burmecians are Medium creatures, and have no bonuses or penalties due to their size.

traits.name: Type
traits.text: Burmecians are Humanoid creatures with the burmecian subtype.

traits.name: Base Speed
traits.text: Burmecians have a base speed of 30 feet.

traits.name: Languages
traits.text: Burmecians begin play speaking Common and Burmecian. Burmecian with high Intelligence scores can choose from the following: Draconic, Dwarven, Elvaan, Galkan, Giant, Goblin, and Orc. See the Linguistics skill page for more information about these languages.

traits.name: Battle-Hardened
traits.text: Incessant drills make defense second nature to all burmecians. Burmecians gain a +1 bonus to CMD.

traits.name: Fearless
traits.text: Burmecians receive a +2 racial bonus on saves against fear spells and effects.

traits.name: Keen Senses
traits.text: Burmecians receive a +2 racial bonus on Perception checks.

traits.name: Natural Jumper
traits.text: Burmecians gain a +4 racial bonus on Acrobatic checks for jumping.

traits.name: Quick Reactions
traits.text: Burmercians gain Improved Initiative as a bonus feat.

traits.name: Darkvision
traits.text: Burmecians can see perfectly in the dark up to 60 feet.

traits.name: Claws
traits.text: A burmecian gains a set of natural claw attacks, dealing 1d4 points of damage. The claws are a primary attack, or a secondary attack if the burmecian is wielding manufactured weapons.

traits.name: Size
traits.text: Dracobaltians are Medium creatures, and have no bonuses or penalties due to their size.

traits.name: Type
traits.text: Dracobaltians are Humanoid creatures with the reptilian subtype.

traits.name: Base Speed
traits.text: Dracobaltian have a base speed of 40 feet on land.

traits.name: Languages
traits.text: Dracobaltian begin play speaking Common and Draconese. Dracobaltian with high Intelligence can choose bonus languages from the following: Draconic, Giant, Ignan, Numish, Seeq, Terran.

traits.name: Stability
traits.text: Dracobaltians receive a +4 racial bonus to their Combat Maneuver Defense when resisting a bull rush or trip attempt while standing on the ground.

traits.name: Leathery-skinned
traits.text: A dracobaltian’s leathery hide grants a +1 bonus to natural armor.

traits.name: Keen Senses
traits.text: Dracobaltians receive a +2 racial bonus on Perception checks.

traits.name: Claws
traits.text: Dracobaltians gain a natural set of claw attacks, dealing 1d4 points of damage. The claws are a primary attack, or a secondary attack if the dracobaltian is wielding manufactured weapons.

traits.name: Lesser Blindsight
traits.text: Dracobaltians are naturally blind, but they have blindsight out to 30 feet. A dracobaltian’s blindsight relies on its ability to hear and smell. This ability works as per blindsight, but the creature still needs to make Perception checks in order to notice creatures within the range of its lesser blindsight ability.

traits.name: Scent
traits.text: Dracobaltians have an enhanced sense of smell and gain the scent special ability.

traits.name: Unsocialable
traits.text: Dracobaltians tend to be aggressive to other races than themselves, they suffer a -4 penalty on Diplomacy checks when dealing with other races.

traits.name: Size
traits.text: Garif are Medium creatures and have no bonuses or penalties due to their size.

traits.name: Type
traits.text: Garif are Humanoid creatures with the garif subtype.

traits.name: Base Speed
traits.text: Garif have a base speed of 30 feet on land.

traits.name: Languages
traits.text: Garif begin play speaking Common and Garif. Garif with high Intelligence scores can choose from the following: Draconic, Dwarven, Elvaan, Galkan, Giant, Goblin, and Orc. See the Linguistics skill page for more information about these languages.

traits.name: Bond to the Land
traits.text: Choosing to cherish and look after the land they settle on, garif are often much more at home within those lands. Pick deserts or plains, garif gain a +2 dodge bonus to AC when in that chosen terrain. This choice is made at character creation, and cannot be changed.

traits.name: Masked
traits.text: Garif wear masks in remembrance of their vows, of the commitment to peace that ended their warrior empire. A masked garif gains a +1 bonus to all saving throws.

traits.name: Animal Herder
traits.text: Garif receive a +2 racial bonus on Handle Animal checks.

traits.name: Keen Senses
traits.text: Garif receive a +2 racial bonus on Perception checks.

traits.name: Pastoralist
traits.text: Garif spend their lives at common tasks. A garif receives one skill rank each level to place into one of the following skills: Craft (any), Knowledge (nature), Profession (any pastoral, e.g. farmer, herbalist, midwife, shepherd, etc.), or Survival. The chosen skill is a class skill.

traits.name: Weapon Familiarity
traits.text: Garif are proficient with the longspear, shortspear, javelin, and boar spear.

traits.name: Low-light Vision
traits.text: Garif can see twice as far as a hume in starlight, moonlight, torchlight, and similar conditions of poor illumination. He retains the ability to distinguish color and detail under these conditions.

traits.name: Size
traits.text: Garleans are Medium creatures and have no bonuses or penalties due to their size.

traits.name: Type
traits.text: Garleans are Humanoid creatures with the garlean subtype.

traits.name: Base Speed
traits.text: Garleans have a base speed of 30 feet.

traits.name: Languages
traits.text: Garleans begin play speaking Common. Garleans with high Intelligence scores can choose from the following: Elvaan, Galkan, Goblin, Lalafellan, and Mithran. See the Linguistics skill page for more information about these languages.

traits.name: Fearless
traits.text: Garleans gain a +2 racial bonus on all saving throws against fear effects.

traits.name: Hardy
traits.text: Garleans gain a +2 racial bonus on saving throws against poison, spells, and spell-like abilities.

traits.name: Magitek Training
traits.text: Garleans gain a +4 dodge bonus to AC against constructs of the robot subtype and magiteks.

traits.name: Keen Senses
traits.text: Garleans receive a +2 racial bonus on Perception checks.

traits.name: Noble Upbringing
traits.text: Garleans take great pride in their history, culture, and government. They receive a +2 bonus on Knowledge (nobility) and Knowledge (history) checks and treat these skills as class skills.

traits.name: Sovereignty of The Nation
traits.text: Garleans are highly efficient with firearms. They can gain Firearms (Simple) or a single Gun Arm Exotic Weapon Proficiency.

traits.name: Technologically Advanced
traits.text: Garleans are very proficient with all things technology. They gain a +2 racial bonus on Knowledge (Technology), Repair, and any one Craft skill that involves building something technological.

traits.name: Third Eye (Su)
traits.text: Garleans, while magically inept, can physically open a third eye in their forehead, which shines like a white gem, and are able to use detect magic at will as a spell-like ability (caster level equal to the garlean‘s class level).

traits.name: Magic Ineptitude
traits.text: Garleans are inept with magic. They are unable to obtain a magic pool nor can they use spell-trigger items, spell-completion items, command word activated item, or use activated items. Garleans can use alchemical items and may activate and deactivate their magic weapons and armor without issue as well as gain bonuses from static magical wondrous items and rings like belts of giant strength.

traits.name: Size
traits.text: Genomes are Medium creatures and thus receive no bonuses or penalties due to their size.

traits.name: Type
traits.text: Genomes are humanoids with the genome subtype.

traits.name: Base Speed
traits.text: Genomes have a base speed of 30 feet.

traits.name: Languages
traits.text: Genomes begin play Common. Genomes with high Intelligence scores can choose any languages they want. See the Linguistics skill page for more information about these languages.

traits.name: Reborn Spirit
traits.text: Many of the souls within genomes have experienced death at least once granting them a strange resilience. Genomes gain a +2 racial bonus to saving throws against Death spells and effects.

traits.name: Sneaky
traits.text: Genomes are adept at infiltrating other worlds. Genomes gain a +4 racial bonus on Stealth checks.

traits.name: Technological Instinct
traits.text: Many genomes who awaken in a Genome village have an inherently advanced understanding of technology. Genomes gain Technologist as a bonus feat and always treat Knowledge (Technology) as a class skill.

traits.name: Dexterous Tail
traits.text: Genomes have a long, flexible tail that can be used to carry objects. They cannot wield weapons with their tails, but they can retrieve small, stowed objects carried on their persons as a swift action.

traits.name: Ideal Vessel
traits.text: Engineered for perfection, a genome’s class level is considered to be 1 level higher for the purpose of determining the DC of the genome’s class abilities.

traits.name: Isolated
traits.text: Most of a genome’s life after “awakening”, is spent around soulless genomes, making it hard to learn to express any sort of emotion or empathy, taking a -2 penalty on all Diplomacy checks. A humanoid’s starting attitude towards genomes is one step worse than normal.

traits.name: Size
traits.text: Gria are Medium creatures and have no bonuses or penalties due to their size.

traits.name: Type
traits.text: Gria are Humanoid creatures with the gria subtype.

traits.name: Base Speed
traits.text: Gria have a base speed of 30 feet on land. While gria wings are too small to provide true flight, the same magic that empowers dragons allows gria to achieve limited flight for short periods of time while wearing light or no armor and carrying no more than a light load. A gria can fly with clumsy maneuverability a number of rounds at a time equal to her Constitution bonus. A gria can attempt to fly for longer durations by making Constitution check each additional round of flight (DC 10 + 2 per extra round). A gria’s natural fly speed is equal to her base land speed. After flying, a gria must rest a number of rounds equal to twice the number of rounds spent flying before flying again.

traits.name: Languages
traits.text: Gria begin play speaking Common and Draconic. Gria with high Intelligence scores can choose from the following: Banganese, Giant, Goblin, Ignan, Seeq, Terran. See the Linguistics skill page for more information about these languages.

traits.name: Fearless
traits.text: Gria receive a +2 racial bonus on saves against fear spells and effects.

traits.name: Stubborn
traits.text: Gria gain a +2 racial bonus on Will saving throws to resist spells and spell-like abilities of the illusion school. In addition, if a gria fails such a save, it receives another save 1 round later to prematurely end the effect (assuming the spell or spell-like ability has a duration greater than 1 round). This second save is made at the same DC as the first. If the gria has a similar ability from another source, it can only use one of these abilities per round, but can try the other on the second round if the first reroll ability fails.

traits.name: Athleticism
traits.text: Gria are naturally fit and nimble. They receive a +2 racial bonus on Acrobatics checks.

traits.name: Diplomatic
traits.text: Gria receive a +2 racial bonus on Diplomacy checks.

traits.name: Survivalist
traits.text: Gria receive a +2 racial bonus on Survival checks.

traits.name: Martial Background
traits.text: Gria receive the Weapon Focus feat for free at first level, and may apply it to any single weapon they are proficient in.

traits.name: Destructive
traits.text: Gria receive a +2 racial bonus on sunder combat maneuver checks.

traits.name: Weapon Familiarity
traits.text: Gria are proficient with the knight sword and longbow (including composite).

traits.name: Low-Light Vision
traits.text: Gria can see twice as far as humes in conditions of dim light.

traits.name: Size
traits.text: Guados are Medium creatures and thus receive no bonuses or penalties due to their size.

traits.name: Type
traits.text: Guados are Humanoids with the guado subtype.

traits.name: Base Speed
traits.text: Guados have a base speed of 35 feet.

traits.name: Languages
traits.text: Guados begin play speaking Common and Guado. Guados with high Intelligence scores can choose from the following for their bonus languages: Al Bhed, Draconic, Elvaan, Lalafell, Numish, Ronsaur, or Vieran.

traits.name: Deathless Spirit
traits.text: Guados are creatures that are attuned to the bridges between life and death, being sensitive to their ebbs and flows, yet resistant to their negative effects. Being living creatures, the forces of death and undeath have less sway over them than other mortals. They gain Shadow Resistance 5. In addition, they do not lose hit points when they gain a negative level, and they gain a +2 racial bonus on saving throws against death effects, energy drain, and spells or spell-like abilities of the necromancy or dark spell varieties.

traits.name: Skill Bonuses
traits.text: Being associated with the powers of life and death makes one hard to read, and by extension hard to fool. This is only further exacerbated by the sometimes lyrical, poetic, or unsettling ways guados tend to speak. Guados gain a +2 racial bonus to Bluff and Sense Motive skills.

traits.name: Skill Training
traits.text: Knowledge of the ways of life and death, bridges between the two, and the aspects of undeath are core to the beliefs and the traditions of the guado. Guados always treat Knowledge (Planes) and Knowledge (Religion) as class skills.

traits.name: Detect Undead (Sp)
traits.text: Guados can make use of detect undead as a constant spell-like ability (the caster level is equal to the guado’s character level).

traits.name: Elemental Summoner
traits.text: Choose one of the following elemental subtypes—earth, fire, ice, lightning, water, wind. When summoning a creature with the chosen subtype with a summon spell, increase the duration of that spell by 2 rounds. This choice is made at character creation, and can only be changed with retraining.

traits.name: Moderate Fleetness
traits.text: Guados’ long limbs allow them to run and swim faster than what others expect of them, but their slender frames only make these advantages go so far. Guados gain a +5 foot bonus to their base land speed (this is already added to their Base Speed above), and guados who have a Swim speed increase it by +5 foot.

traits.name: Size
traits.text: Hypellos are Medium creatures and thus receive no bonuses or penalties due to their size.

traits.name: Type
traits.text: Hypellos are Humanoid creatures with a hypello subtype.

traits.name: Base Speed
traits.text: Hypellos have a base speed of 20 feet, but their speed is never modified by armor or encumbrance. Though due to their life near and within water, they have a swim speed of 30 feet.

traits.name: Languages
traits.text: Hypellos begin play speaking Common and Hypello. Hypellos with high Intelligence scores can choose from the following: Moogle, Goblin, Sylvan, Dwarven. See the Linguistics skill page for more information about these languages.

traits.name: Camouflage
traits.text: Hypellos receive a +4 racial bonus on Stealth checks in marshes and forested areas.

traits.name: Hardy
traits.text: Hypellos gain a +2 racial bonus on saving throws against poison, spells, and spell-like abilities.

traits.name: Amphibians
traits.text: Hypellos begin with the Amphibious racial trait, allowing them to breathe both air and water.

traits.name: Animal Empathy
traits.text: Hypellos gain a +2 racial bonus to all Handle Animal checks made to influence animals.

traits.name: Rider
traits.text: Hypellos gain a +2 racial bonus on Ride checks.

traits.name: Ride ze Shoopuf?
traits.text: Hypellos treat Handle Animal and Ride as class skills.

traits.name: Swamp Stride
traits.text: A hypello can move through difficult terrain at its normal speed while within a swamp. Magically altered terrain affects a hypello normally.

traits.name: Swim
traits.text: Hypellos have a swim speed of 30 feet and gain the +8 racial bonus on swim checks that a swim speed normally grants.

traits.name: Darkvision
traits.text: Hypellos can see perfectly in the dark up to 60 feet.

traits.name: Poor Communication
traits.text: Due to their vocal patterns and childish demeanor, hypellos gain a -2 to Diplomacy and Intimidation checks against all other races.

traits.name: Size
traits.text: Immortals are Medium creatures and thus receive no bonuses or penalties due to their size.

traits.name: Type
traits.text: Immortals are Humanoid creatures with the immortal subtype.

traits.name: Base Speed
traits.text: Immortals have a base speed of 30 feet.

traits.name: Languages
traits.text: Immortals begin play speaking Common. Immortals with high Intelligence scores can choose from the following: Celestial, Draconic, Galkan, Goblin, Lalafellan, Mithran, and Orc. See the Linguistics skill page for more information about these languages.

traits.name: Immunity to Death
traits.text: Immortals are immune to death effects and spells, such as Death.

traits.name: Immunity to Undeath
traits.text: Immortals are immune to any effects that would raise them as an undead creature, such as Animate Dead.

traits.name: Integrated
traits.text: Immortals gain a +1 racial bonus on Bluff, Disguise, and Knowledge (local) checks.

traits.name: Long-Lived
traits.text: Immortals remember bits of their long lives. As a result, they can select up to four Knowledge skills as class skills.

traits.name: Sociable
traits.text: When immortals attempt to change a creature’s attitude with a Diplomacy check and fail by 5 or more, they can try to influence the creature a second time even if 24 hours have not passed.

traits.name: Linking
traits.text: As a full-round action, once per day, immortals can link with a non-immortal spellcaster (must be willing and only one individual at a time) to gain some of their powers. Doing so allows immortals to cast 1 spell (must be a standard action or less) from the non-immortal spellcaster’s known spell list (the character level of the immortal must be double of a spell level of the spell to learn and must have the mental stat to cast) as a spell-like ability any time during the day.

traits.name: Immortal
traits.text: Immortals do not gain any benefits or penalties for their age category, and generally stop ageing just before middle age. The creature may still die due to diseases and other natural causes, but age does not harm them. The creature is also immune to any attacks or effects that would age them such as Withering.

traits.name: Spirit-Tapped
traits.text: Immortals are rather resistant to permanent death. When their negative hit point total drops to or below their Constitution score, they gain 1 permanent negative level instead of dying. Whilst in this “dead” state they gain fast healing equal to half their character level until back to 0 hit points or higher. This negative level stacks up to their character level – 1. If the maximum number of negative levels are reached, they instead remain inert until cured of a negative level. Creatures with this trait can still be killed if their body parts are removed, or die from effects such as Vorpal, and if not reattached will keep the immortal in their dead state. Having their Constitution score reduced to 0 will also kill them.

traits.name: Undying
traits.text: An Immortal responds slightly differently from other living creatures when reduced to 0 hit points. When an Immortal is at 0 hit points they are disabled and can only take a single move action or standard action in each round, but strenuous activity does not risk further injury. When their health drops to -1 or lower they automatically stabilize, but can still die from further damage.

traits.name: Magic Ineptitude
traits.text: Immortals are inept with magic. They are unable to obtain a magic pool nor can they use spell-trigger items, spell-completion items, command word activated item, or use activated items except through their linking (see above). Immortals can use alchemical items and may activate and deactivate their magic weapons and armor without issue as well as gain bonuses from static magical wondrous items and rings like belts of giant strength.

traits.name: Not of this Plane
traits.text: An immortal’s connection to the Material Plane can be severed and altered, causing a weakness to occur where they did not anticipate. If subject to a successful dispel check (DC 10 + their hit die + their Wisdom modifier), without any current active effects, they are knocked unconscious for a number of rounds equal to the CL of the enemy who used the dispel. Likewise, any Immortal caught in an anti-magic field or similar effect is knocked unconscious until their body leaves the vicinity of the effect. Immortals are also affected by any spells that negatively affect outsiders or summoned creatures.

traits.name: Size
traits.text: Lambkins are Small creatures and thus gain a +1 size bonus to their AC, a +1 size bonus on attack rolls, a –1 penalty to their Combat Maneuver Bonus and Combat Maneuver Defense, and a +4 size bonus on Stealth checks.

traits.name: Type
traits.text: Lambkins are humanoids with the lambkin subtype.

traits.name: Base Speed
traits.text: (Slow Speed) Lambkins have a base speed of 20 feet on land and are always considered to be floating a couple of feet off the ground.

traits.name: Languages
traits.text: Lambkins begin play speaking Common and Lambkin. Lambkins with high Intelligence scores can choose from the following: Galkan, Giant, Goblin, Lalafellan, and Orc. See the Linguistics skill page for more information about these languages.

traits.name: Magic Resistant
traits.text: Lambkins are particularly resistant to magic. They gain spell resistance equal to 6 + their character level.

traits.name: Magic Expert
traits.text: Lambkins value knowledge and learning about the field of magic. They gain a +2 racial bonus on Knowledge (Arcana) and Spellcraft checks.

traits.name: Auto-Float
traits.text: Lambkins are always considered to have the Float status. Without it, they can only crawl 5 feet per movement action. Lambkins that are subjected to a dispel effect (the float effect has a caster level equal to the lambkin’s character level) lose this float effect for 1 round. Lambkins in anti-magic areas automatically lose the float status until they leave the area.

traits.name: Magic Aptitude
traits.text: Lambkins gain a +2 racial bonus on caster level checks made to overcome spell resistance and a +2 racial bonus on dispel checks.

traits.name: Magick Focus
traits.text: Lambkins gain a +2 racial bonus on concentration checks made to cast spells defensively.

traits.name: Low-Light Vision
traits.text: Lambkins can see twice as far as humes in conditions of dim light.

traits.name: Type
traits.text: Humanoid Plant: Mandragoras are unique creatures, possessing traits of both humanoids and plants. A mandragora is treated as both humanoid and plant for the purposes of effects that target a specific type of creature. Unlike most plants, a mandragora is not immune to mind-affecting effects, poison, paralysis, polymorph, or stunning.

traits.name: Size
traits.text: Mandragoras are Small creatures and thus gain a +1 size bonus to their AC, a +1 size bonus on attack rolls, a –1 penalty to their Combat Maneuver Bonus and Combat Maneuver Defense, and a +4 size bonus on Stealth checks.

traits.name: Base Speed
traits.text: Mandragoras have a base speed of 20 feet.

traits.name: Languages
traits.text: Mandragoras begin play speaking Common and Mandragoran. Mandragoras with high Intelligence scores can choose from the following: Draconic, Dwarven, Elvaan, Galkan, Giant, Goblin, and Sylvan. See the Linguistics skill page for more information about these languages.

traits.name: Elemental Resistance
traits.text: With such an attachment to the earth, mandragoras don’t take as much damage from it. Mandragoras gain resistance 5 against earth damage.

traits.name: Hydrated Vitality
traits.text: Mandragoras gain fast healing 2 for 1 round anytime they submerge completely within a body of natural salt water, fresh water, or brackish water. Stagnant, poisoned, or trapped water (such as water within an artificial pit or a bag of holding) does not activate this ability. Mandragoras can heal up to 2 hit points per level per day with this ability, after which it ceases to function.

traits.name: Natural Armor
traits.text: Their plant-like nature has gifted mandragoras with a fibrous, stiff skin much like bark. This grants them a +1 natural armor bonus.

traits.name: Plant Resistance
traits.text: While technically a plant, a mandragora has more in common with most humanoids. They gain a +2 racial bonus on saving throws against mind-affecting effects (charms, compulsions, phantasms, patterns, and morale effects), paralysis, poison, and polymorph effects. They are immune to sleep effects.

traits.name: Camouflage
traits.text: Mandragoras gain a +4 racial bonus on Stealth checks while in marshes, jungles, or forested terrains.

traits.name: In Tune with the Earth
traits.text: Mandragoras are treated as 1 level higher when casting spells with the earth descriptor. This ability does not give mandragoras early access to level-based powers; it only affects powers that they could already use without this ability.

traits.name: Spell-Like Ability (Sp
traits.text: Mandragoras can use photosynthesis once per day as a spell-like ability (caster level equal to the mandragora’s class level).

traits.name: Terrain Stride
traits.text: Mandragoras ignore natural difficult terrain within forests and move at their normal speed within said environments. Magically altered terrain affects them normally.

traits.name: Shriek
traits.text: Once per day as a standard action, a mandragora can give voice to an unsettling shriek. All creatures within a 30-foot spread of a shrieking mandragora must make a Will save (DC 10 + half of the mandragora’s character level + its Wisdom modifier) or become nauseated for 1d4 rounds. This is a sonic, mind-affecting ability.

traits.name: Weapon Familiarity
traits.text: Mandragorans treat any weapon with the word “mandragoran” in its name as a martial weapon.

traits.name: Bioluminescence
traits.text: At will, a mandragora can cause any part of his body to glow, giving off light as a torch.

traits.name: Sunlight Sustenance
traits.text: A mandragora does not eat food, but must consume water like all living things. As long as it receives at least six hours of sunlight per day, a mandragora requires only 1/4th the water a normal humanoid would. A mandragora deprived of adequate sunlight for more than two days at a time becomes fatigued until it gets at least six hours of sunlight. If it does not get sunlight for more than a week, it becomes exhausted until it gets at least six hours of sunlight. A one hour exposure to a daylight spell will fulfill a mandragora’s daily needs.

traits.name: Low-Light Vision
traits.text: Mandragoras can see twice as far as humes in conditions of dim light.

traits.name: Temperature Vulnerability
traits.text: A mandragora has trouble regulating its body temperature. Mandragoras have a –4 penalty to Fortitude saves made against environmental effects.

traits.name: Vulnerable to Fire
traits.text: Mandragoras take 150% as much damage as normal from fire attacks, unless they are immune to fire via other special defenses. Mandragoras also suffer a -2 penalty on saving throws versus spells and effects that have the fire subschool or deal fire damage and grant the opponents a +2 bonus to caster level checks when attacking with these effects.

traits.name: Weakened by Cold
traits.text: As the winter slows the growth of trees, it also tires and weakens the mandragora. If a mandragora suffers ice damage, it withers and wilts, needing to make a Fortitude save equal to 10 + the half the damage suffered. Failure to save means the mandragora is staggered for 1 round.

traits.name: Size
traits.text: Moombas are Small creatures and thus gain a +1 size bonus to their AC, a +1 size bonus on attack rolls, a –1 penalty to their Combat Maneuver Bonus and Combat Maneuver Defense, and a +4 size bonus on Stealth checks.

traits.name: Type
traits.text: Moombas are Monstrous Humanoid creatures with a moomba subtype.

traits.name: Base Speed
traits.text: Moombas have a base speed of 40 feet.

traits.name: Languages
traits.text: Moombas cannot fully speak any language, only being able to converse through body language and specific words, though they can understand languages fully if they spend the time to learn and can even write in those languages. Moombas can communicate flawlessly with other moomba or shumi. Moombas must spend double the ranks to learn a new language, but they may never speak it fully. Moombas begin play understanding common. Moombas with high Intelligence scores can choose from the following: Undercommon, moogle. See the Linguistics skill page for more information about these languages.

traits.name: Desert Runner
traits.text: Moombas receive a +4 racial bonus on Constitution checks and Fortitude saves to avoid fatigue and exhaustion, as well as any other ill effects from running, forced marches, starvation, thirst, and hot or cold environments.

traits.name: Stability
traits.text: Moombas receive a +4 racial bonus to their CMD when resisting bull rush or trip attempts while standing on the ground.

traits.name: Choco / Mog buddies
traits.text: Moombas are incredibly close with moogles and chocobos, gaining a +4 bonus on any Diplomacy, Bluff, Wild Empathy, and Ride checks with them.

traits.name: Prehensile Tail
traits.text: Members of this race have a long, flexible tail that can be used to carry objects. They cannot wield weapons with their tails, but they can retrieve small, stowed objects carried on their persons as a swift action.

traits.name: Bite
traits.text: Moombas have a dangerous natural bite attack, dealing 1d3 points of damage. The bite is a primary attack, or a secondary attack if the creature is wielding manufactured weapons.

traits.name: Claws
traits.text: Moombas have claws both on their hands and receive two claw attacks that deal 1d3 points of damage. These are primary natural attacks that use their upper arms.

traits.name: Slapping Tail
traits.text: Moombas have a tail they can use to make attacks of opportunity with a reach of 5 feet. The tail is a secondary natural attack that deals 1d4 points of damage plus the user’s Strength modifier.

traits.name: Darkvision
traits.text: Moombas have darkvision with a range of 60 feet.

traits.name: Broken Language
traits.text: Moombas cannot speak any language fully and so take a -4 when using Diplomacy, except against moombas, shumi, moogles, and chocobos.

traits.name: Vocal Failure
traits.text: When casting spells with vocal components, moombas have to overcome their lack of words, they must succeed a linguistics check (DC 15 + double Spell Level) or lose the spell.

traits.name: Size
traits.text: Mutants are Medium creatures and have no bonuses or penalties due to their size.

traits.name: Type
traits.text: Mutants are Humanoid creatures with the mutant subtype.

traits.name: Base Speed
traits.text: Mutants have a base speed of 30 feet on land.

traits.name: Languages
traits.text: Mutants begin play speaking Common. Mutants with high Intelligence scores can choose from the following: Draconic, Dwarven, Elvaan, Galkan, Giant, Goblin, and Orc. See the Linguistics skill page for more information about these languages.

traits.name: Variable Resistance
traits.text: Mutants must roll a 1d6 on creation (1-Earth, 2-Fire, 3-Ice, 4-Lightning, 5-Water, 6-Wind) and gains that elemental resistance 5.

traits.name: Keen Senses
traits.text: Mutants receive a +2 racial bonus on Perception checks.

traits.name: Spell-Like Ability (Sp)
traits.text: Mutants can choose a 1st-level blue mage spell and cast it once per day as a spell-like ability (caster level equal to the mutant’s class level). In addition, if the mutant is also a blue mage, he gains a +2 bonus on Knowledge skill checks on learning spells.

traits.name: Variable Mutant Abilities
traits.text: Mutants gain a random mutant ability by rolling a 1d100 on the table below, once upon creation. Any abilities that grant spells or spell-like abilities are treated as having a caster level equal to the mutant’s character level. Mutants may roll on the alternative physical features by rolling a 1d100 as well.

traits.name: Variable Stats
traits.text: Mutants experience unpredictable physical and mental growth as they advance. At each character level beyond 1st, a mutant gains a +1 bonus to a randomly determined ability score. Roll 1d6 to determine the affected ability score (1 = Strength, 2 = Dexterity, 3 = Constitution, 4 = Intelligence, 5 = Wisdom, 6 = Charisma). A mutant may gain a maximum of +6 total bonuses to any single ability score from this trait. If a roll would grant a bonus to an ability score that has already reached this maximum, reroll until a valid result is obtained. This racial trait replaces the standard ability score increases gained at every 4th character level.

traits.name: Darkvision
traits.text: Mutants can see perfectly in the dark up to 60 feet.

traits.name: Low-light Vision
traits.text: A mutant can see twice as far as a hume in starlight, moonlight, torchlight, and similar conditions of poor illumination. He retains the ability to distinguish color and detail under these conditions.

traits.name: Type
traits.text: Nu mous are Humanoid creatures with the nu mou subtype.

traits.name: Size
traits.text: Nu mous are Small creatures and thus gain a +1 size bonus to their AC, a +1 size bonus on attack rolls, a –1 penalty to their Combat Maneuver Bonus and Combat Maneuver Defense, and a +4 size bonus on Stealth checks.

traits.name: Base Speed
traits.text: (Slow Speed) Nu mous have a base speed of 20 feet.

traits.name: Languages
traits.text: Nu mous begin play speaking Common and Numish. Nu mous with high Intelligence scores can choose from the following: Banganese, Celestial, Draconic, Giant, Moogle, Sylvan and Vieran. See the Linguistics skill page for more information about these languages.

traits.name: Sagacious
traits.text: Nu mous receive a +2 racial bonus on any two Knowledge skills. These two knowledge skills count as class skills for the nu mou.

traits.name: Well-Spoken
traits.text: Nu mous receive a +2 racial bonus on Diplomacy and Handle Animal checks.

traits.name: Low-Light Vision
traits.text: Nu mous can see twice as far as humes in conditions of dim light.

traits.name: Poor Swimmer
traits.text: Nu mous take a –4 penalty on Swim checks.

traits.name: Size
traits.text: Palicos are Small creatures and thus gain a +1 size bonus to their AC, a +1 size bonus on attack rolls, a –1 penalty to their Combat Maneuver Bonus and Combat Maneuver Defense, and a +4 size bonus on Stealth checks.

traits.name: Type
traits.text: Palicos are Humanoid creatures with the feline subtype.

traits.name: Base Speed
traits.text: Palicos are fast for their size, and have a base speed of 30 feet.

traits.name: Languages
traits.text: Palicos begin play speaking Common and either Mithran or Ronsaur. Palicos with high Intelligence scores can choose from the following: Abyssal, Celestial, Elvaan, Galkan, Goblin, and Orc. See the Linguistics skill page for more information about these languages.

traits.name: Heavy Lifter
traits.text: Palicos are used to carrying heavy equipment and as such, are treated as if their Strength score was 4 points higher for encumbrance.

traits.name: Nimble Faller
traits.text: Palicos have an amazing sense of balance and keen knowledge of their own center of gravity. Palicos land on their feet even when they take lethal damage from a fall and take damage as if the fall were 10 feet shorter than it actually is. Furthermore, palicos gain a +1 bonus to their CMD against trip combat maneuvers.

traits.name: Feline Conversationalist
traits.text: Palicos may comprehend and communicate at will with all feline animals.

traits.name: Nimble
traits.text: Palicos use their Dexterity to modify Climb and Swim checks.

traits.name: Sprinter
traits.text: Palicos gain a 10-foot racial bonus to their speed when using the charge, run, or withdraw actions.

traits.name: Bite
traits.text: Palicos have a primary natural attack: a bite that inflicts 1d3 points of damage

traits.name: Claws
traits.text: Palicos have two primary natural attacks: two claws that inflict 1d3 points of damage each.

traits.name: Cat Senses
traits.text: In addition to having low-light vision, palicos have the scent ability.

traits.name: Non-threatening
traits.text: Palicos are too cute for their own good and suffer a -4 penalty on Intimidation checks.

traits.name: Easily Distracted
traits.text: Palicos turn their head at any distraction and suffer a -2 penalty on Concentration checks.

traits.name: Naïve
traits.text: Palicos love a good ear scratch, often trusting too quickly and suffer a -2 penalty on Sense Motive checks.

traits.name: Type
traits.text: PuPu are aberrations (humanoids).

traits.name: Size
traits.text: PuPu are Small creatures and thus gain a +1 size bonus to their AC, a +1 size bonus on attack rolls, a –1 penalty to their Combat Maneuver Bonus and Combat Maneuver Defense, and a +4 size bonus on Stealth checks.

traits.name: Base Speed
traits.text: PuPu have a base speed of 20 feet.

traits.name: Languages
traits.text: PuPu begin play speaking Common and PuPon. PuPu with high Intelligence scores can choose from the following: Draconic, Dwarven, Elvaan, Galkan, Giant, Goblin, and Sylvan. See the Linguistics skill page for more information about these languages.

traits.name: Alien Mindset
traits.text: The PuPu are too intelligent for their own good. They gain a +2 racial bonus on saving throws against mind-affecting effects (charms, compulsions, illusions, phantasms, patterns, and morale effects), antagonize, confusion, and berserk.

traits.name: Technological Savant
traits.text: PuPu gain a +2 racial bonus on Knowledge (Technology or Engineering) and Repair skill checks.

traits.name: Technologist
traits.text: PuPu gain the Technologist feat at 1st level.

traits.name: Darkvision
traits.text: PuPu can see perfectly in the dark up to 60 feet.

traits.name: Size
traits.text: Qus are Medium creatures and thus receive no bonuses or penalties due to their size.

traits.name: Type
traits.text: Qus are humanoids with the qu subtype.

traits.name: Base Speed
traits.text: Qus have a base speed of 30 feet.

traits.name: Languages
traits.text: Qus begin play speaking Common and Queran. Qus with high Intelligence scores can choose from the following: Galkan, Giant, Goblin, Lalafellan, and Orc. See the Linguistics skill page for more information about these languages.

traits.name: Strong Stomach
traits.text: Qus gain a +4 racial bonus to saving throws against poison and sap status effects due to their unique biology.

traits.name: Expert Chefs
traits.text: Qus are renowned chefs of the culinary world. They gain a +2 racial bonus to Profession (Chef) skill checks.

traits.name: Great Lungs
traits.text: Qus receive the Endurance feat for free at first level.

traits.name: Local Quisine
traits.text: Qus are adept at picking up local ingredients for their dishes and so gain a +2 racial bonus on Knowledge (Nature) and Knowledge (Local) checks, the qu also treat these as class skills.

traits.name: Weapon Familiarity
traits.text: Qus are proficient with the chef weapons group and the Qu Battle Fork.

traits.name: Scent
traits.text: Qus have the best noses for sniffing out new ingredients. Qus gain the scent ability.

traits.name: Size
traits.text: Roegadyns are Medium creatures and thus receive no bonuses or penalties due to their size.

traits.name: Type
traits.text: Roegadyns are humanoids with the roegadyn subtype.

traits.name: Base Speed
traits.text: Roegadyns have a base speed of 30 feet.

traits.name: Languages
traits.text: Roegadyns begin play speaking Common and Roegadyn. Roegadyns with high Intelligence scores can choose from the following: Dwarven, Elvaan, Giant, Goblin, Lalafellan, and Orc. See the Linguistics skill page for more information about these languages.

traits.name: Hardy
traits.text: Roegadyns receive a +2 racial bonus on saving throws against poison, spells, and spell-like abilities.

traits.name: Powerful Build
traits.text: The physical stature of roegadyns lets them function in many ways as if they were one size category larger. Whenever a roegadyn is subject to a size modifier or special size modifier for a Combat Maneuver Bonus or Combat Maneuver Defense (such as during grapple checks, bull rush attempts, and trip attempts), the roegadyn is treated as one size larger if doing so is advantageous to him. A roegadyn is also considered to be one size larger when determining whether a creature’s special attacks based on size (such as grab or swallow whole) can affect him. The benefits of this racial trait don’t stack with the effects of powers, abilities, and spells that change the subject’s size category (including Giant Weapon Wielder).

traits.name: Stability
traits.text: Roegadyns receive a +4 bonus to their Combat Maneuver Defense when resisting a bull rush or trip attempt while standing on the ground.

traits.name: Imposing Figure
traits.text: Roegadyns are intimidating without trying. They gain a +2 racial bonus to Intimidate checks.

traits.name: Cornered Fury
traits.text: Roegadyns that are reduced to half their hit points or fewer and have no conscious ally within 30 feet, they gain a +2 racial bonus on melee attack rolls and to Armor Class.

traits.name: Low-Light Vision
traits.text: Roegadyns have low-light vision allowing them to see twice as far as humes in dim light.

traits.name: Size
traits.text: Ronsos are Medium creatures and thus receive no bonuses or penalties due to their size.

traits.name: Type
traits.text: Ronsos are humanoids with the ronso subtype.

traits.name: Base Speed
traits.text: Ronsos have a base speed of 30 feet.

traits.name: Languages
traits.text: Ronsos begin play speaking Common and Ronsaur. Ronsos with high Intelligence scores can choose from the following: Galkan, Giant, Goblin, Lalafellan, and Orc. See the Linguistics skill page for more information about these languages

traits.name: Arctic Fur
traits.text: Ronsos are immune to environmental damage from cold weather (below 40° F degrees). In conditions of extreme cold (below 0° F degrees), ronsos suffer the normal conditions for cold weather, not the harsher conditions for extreme cold. In addition, ronsos gain Ice Resistance 5.

traits.name: Fearless
traits.text: Ronsos receive a +2 racial bonus on saves against fear spells and effects.

traits.name: Intimidating Build
traits.text: Ronsos are intimidating even when they don’t mean to be. Ronsos gain a +2 racial bonus on intimidation checks.

traits.name: Mountaineers
traits.text: Ronsos are adept climbers, gaining a +2 racial bonus on Climb checks. In addition, they are immune to altitude sickness and do not lose their Dexterity bonus to AC when making Climb checks or Acrobatics checks to cross narrow or slippery surfaces.

traits.name: Survivalist
traits.text: Ronsos are hunters and can hunt in the best and worst of weather conditions. They gain a +2 racial bonus on all Survival checks.

traits.name: Gore
traits.text: Ronsos can use their horns as a natural attack that deals 1d6 points of damage. This is a primary natural attack.

traits.name: Darkvision
traits.text: All ronsos can see perfectly in the dark up to 60 feet.

traits.name: Stand On Your Own Feet
traits.text: Ronsos do not do well when traveling by means other than their own two feet. They take a –2 penalty to all Fly and Ride checks.

traits.name: Size
traits.text: Seeq are Medium creatures and thus receive no bonuses or penalties due to their size.

traits.name: Type
traits.text: Seeq are humanoids with the seeq subtype.

traits.name: Base Speed
traits.text: Seeq have a base speed of 30 feet.

traits.name: Languages
traits.text: Seeq begin play speaking Common and Seeq. Seeq with high Intelligence scores can choose from the following: Banganese, Draconic, Giant, Goblin, Terran, Undercommon. See the Linguistics skill page for more information about these languages.

traits.name: Desert Runner
traits.text: Seeq receive a +4 racial bonus on Constitution checks and Fortitude saves to avoid fatigue and exhaustion, as well as any other ill effects from running, forced marches, starvation, thirst, and hot or cold environments.

traits.name: Hardy
traits.text: Seeq gain a +2 racial bonus on saving throws against poison, spells, and spell-like abilities.

traits.name: Stability
traits.text: Seeq receive a +4 racial bonus to their CMD when resisting bull rush or trip attempts while standing on the ground.

traits.name: Deceptive
traits.text: Seeq learn at an early age it is beneficial for others to perceive them as dull and slow. Seeq gain a +2 racial bonus on Bluff checks that play upon this perception.

traits.name: Perceptive
traits.text: In addition to trusting their senses, Seeq studiously watch those around them, picking up signals others wouldn’t. Seeq gain a +2 racial bonus on Perception and Sense Motive checks.

traits.name: Scavenger
traits.text: Seeq gain a +2 racial bonus on Appraise and Perception checks to find hidden objects (including traps and secret doors), determine whether food is spoiled, or identify a potion by taste.

traits.name: Low-Light Vision
traits.text: Seeq can see twice as far as a hume in starlight, moonlight, torchlight, and similar conditions of poor illumination. He retains the ability to distinguish color and detail under these conditions.

traits.name: Size
traits.text: Seto Lions are Medium creatures and thus receive no bonuses or penalties due to their size.

traits.name: Type
traits.text: Seto Lions are Magical Beast creatures with a seto lion subtype.

traits.name: Base Speed
traits.text: Seto Lions have a base speed of 50 feet.

traits.name: Languages
traits.text: Seto Lions begin play speaking Common and Lionese. Seto Lions with high Intelligence scores can choose any languages they want. See the Linguistics skill page for more information about these languages.

traits.name: Cat’s Luck
traits.text: Once per day, when seto lions make a Reflex saving throw, they can roll the saving throw twice and take the better result. They must decide to use this ability before attempting the saving throw.

traits.name: Altered Slots
traits.text: As seto lions lack proper hands their slots are shifted around. Instead of 2 ring slots they have 2 jewelry slots on their headdress. Instead of a hand slot they have 1 arm wrapping slot. Rings can easily fit the headdress jewelry slots, however, hand items must be made specifically for their race, but do not cost any extra.

traits.name: Skill Bonus
traits.text: Seto Lions gain a +2 racial bonus on Acrobatic checks made with this skill.

traits.name: Skill Training
traits.text: Acrobatics and Climb are always class skills for a seto lion.

traits.name: Everburning Tail
traits.text: Seto Lions of 30 years and older have a tail tip of fire. This fire produces a 10-foot radius of normal light and increases the light level for an additional 10-foot radius beyond that by one step, as well as can deal 1 point of fire damage per round if touching an object as well as being able to set flammable objects on fire. This fire and be turned off and on at will, but cannot alight when wet.

traits.name: Fast
traits.text: Seto Lions gain a +10 foot bonus to their base speed (this is already added to their Base Speed above.)

traits.name: Bite
traits.text: Seto Lions are used to using their fangs as weapons. Seto Lions gain a natural bite attack, dealing 1d3 points of damage. The bite is a primary attack, or a secondary attack if the creature is wielding manufactured weapons.

traits.name: Claws
traits.text: Seto Lions make use of their claws in combat where weapons or magic are not at their disposal. Seto Lions receive two claw attacks that deal 1d4 damage. These are primary natural attacks, or a secondary attack if the creature is wielding manufactured weapons.

traits.name: Jaw Weapons
traits.text: Seto Lions cannot handle weapons normally with their claws, instead they train heavily to use weapons with their jaws. Seto Lions may wield any light or one-handed weapons in their jaws, however, they are unable to wield any with their other appendages.

traits.name: Darkvision
traits.text: Seto Lions can see perfectly in the dark up to 60 feet.

traits.name: Low-Light Vision
traits.text: Seto Lions have low-light vision allowing them to see twice as far as humes in dim light.

traits.name: Quadruped
traits.text: Seto Lions possess 4 legs, ending in claws, granting them a +4 racial bonus to CMD against trip attempts and a +10 foot bonus to their base speed (this is already added to their Base Speed above). As quadrupeds, seto lions are counted as long for size categories and have an increased carrying capacity, 1.5x for medium size (1x for small, 3x for large). Seto lions count their front paws as “hands” for casting purposes.

traits.name: Size
traits.text: Shindroids are Medium creatures and have no bonuses or penalties due to their size.

traits.name: Type
traits.text: Constructed (Ex): Shindroids, are unique creatures, possessing traits of both humanoids and constructs. A Shindroid is treated as both humanoid and construct for the purposes of effects that target a specific type of creature. Unlike most constructs, a Shindroid is not immune to mind-affecting effects, poison, paralysis, bleed, blind, disease, death effects, necromancy effects, and stunning.

traits.name: Base Speed
traits.text: Shindroids have a base speed of 30 feet.

traits.name: Languages
traits.text: Shindroids begin play speaking Common. Shindroids with high Intelligence can choose any languages they want. See the Linguistics skill page for more information about these languages.

traits.name: Composite Plating
traits.text: Shindroids have a +1 natural armor bonus.

traits.name: Robotic Immunities
traits.text: Shindroids are immune to Fatigued, Exhausted, and Sleep status effects, and are immune to fear and emotion-based spells and effects.

traits.name: Part Robot
traits.text: Shindroids receive the Cybertech Savant feat at 1st level.

traits.name: Perceptive
traits.text: Shindroids gain a +2 racial bonus on Perception checks.

traits.name: Natural Weapons
traits.text: Shindroids have a slam attack that deals 1d4 (1d3 if small) points of damage.

traits.name: Darkvision
traits.text: Shindroids have darkvision to a range of 60 feet.

traits.name: Immortal
traits.text: As artificial creatures, shindroids do not gain any benefits or penalties for their age category, and generally stop ageing or are rather built just before middle age. The creature may still die due to diseases and other natural causes, but age does not harm them. The creature is also immune to any attacks or effects that would age them such as Withering.

traits.name: Self-Sustained
traits.text: Shindroids do not eat, drink or breathe. Therefore, they are immune to the effects of starvation, suffocation and thirst. On the other hand, shindroid have no sense of smell or taste, and they cannot benefit from the effects of consumable spells or magic items. A shindroid can still use oils and potions as long as they don’t heal hit points, unless they have the Living Construct feat (see below).

traits.name: Emotionless
traits.text: Shindroids have problems processing emotions properly, and thus take a –4 penalty on Sense Motive checks and can never gain morale bonuses.

traits.name: High Maintenance
traits.text: Shindroids healed by healing spells and effects works at 50% efficiency except spells and effects that grant fast healing. They, however, do not benefit from the Heal skill. But, shindroids can be repaired by the Repair skill.

traits.name: Magic Ineptitude
traits.text: Shindroids are inept with magic. They are unable to obtain MP nor can they use spell-trigger items, spell-completion items, command word activated item, or use activated items. Shindroids can use alchemical items and may activate and deactivate their magic weapons and armor without issue as well as gain bonuses from static magical wondrous items and rings like belts of giant strength.

traits.name: Rejuvenation Cycle
traits.text: A shindroid runs on energy cells that need to rejuvenate regularly. During a 24-hour period, it must shut down for 8 hours to replenish its energy supply. During its rejuvenation cycle, the shindroid is essentially asleep. If it fails to rejuvenate, it suffers a cumulative –1 penalty on attack rolls, ability checks, skill checks, and saving throws each day until it fully recharges itself.

traits.name: Type
traits.text: Tonkins are Humanoid creatures with the tonberry subtype.

traits.name: Size
traits.text: Tonkins are Small creatures and thus gain a +1 size bonus to their AC, a +1 size bonus on attack rolls, a –1 penalty to their Combat Maneuver Bonus and Combat Maneuver Defense, and a +4 size bonus on Stealth checks.

traits.name: Base Speed
traits.text: Tonkins have a base speed of 20 feet on land. Tonkins’ speed are never modified by armor or encumbrance.

traits.name: Languages
traits.text: Tonkins begin play understanding (but not speaking) (see limited telepathy) Common and Tonberry. Tonkins with high Intelligence scores can choose from the following: Aklo, Auran, Draconic, Goblin, Numish, and Sylvan. See the Linguistics skill page for more information about these languages.

traits.name: Fearless
traits.text: Tonkins receive a +2 racial bonus on saves against fear spells and effects.

traits.name: Murderous Aura
traits.text: Tonkins let off an aura that makes most quake at the sight of them. Tonkins gain a +2 racial bonus to intimidation checks.

traits.name: Sneaky
traits.text: Tonkins gain a +4 racial bonus on Stealth checks.

traits.name: Serrated Wound
traits.text: When tonkins damage an opponent with a light piercing melee weapon, they deal an extra 1d4 bleed damage. This ability does not stack with other special abilities, attacks, or items that allow them to deal bleed damage.

traits.name: Low-Light Vision
traits.text: Tonkins can see twice as far as humes in conditions of dim light.

traits.name: Unable to Cast
traits.text: Due to their nature of being mutes, tonkins are unable to cast spells with a vocal component normally without either Silent Spell or Telepathic Spellcaster feat.

traits.name: Size
traits.text: Vargs are Medium creatures and have no bonuses or penalties due to their size.

traits.name: Type
traits.text: Vargs are Humanoid creatures with the varg subtype.

traits.name: Base Speed
traits.text: Vargs have a base speed of 30 feet.

traits.name: Languages
traits.text: Vargs begin play speaking Common and Lupin. Vargs with high Intelligence scores can choose from the following: Draconic, Dwarven, Elvaan, Galkan, Giant, Goblin, and Orc. See the Linguistics skill page for more information about these languages.

traits.name: Fearless
traits.text: Vargs gain a +2 racial bonus on all saving throws against fear effects.

traits.name: Natural Armor
traits.text: Vargs have a +1 natural armor bonus.

traits.name: Lycanthropy Resistance
traits.text: Vargs are immune to the curse of lycanthropy. Varg’s natural attacks count as silver for the purpose of bypassing damage reduction, and a varg may spend a standard action and touch a lycanthrope to give that lycanthrope an insight bonus equal to the half the varg’s level plus his Wisdom modifier (minimum +1) to the target’s check to change back to human form.

traits.name: Keen Senses
traits.text: Vargs receive a +2 racial bonus on Perception checks.

traits.name: Wolf Empathy
traits.text: Vargs receive a +4 racial bonus on Handle Animal and Diplomacy checks when dealing with wolves, dire wolves, or any other wolf subtype.

traits.name: Bite
traits.text: Vargs gain a natural bite attack, dealing 1d4 points of damage. The bite is a primary attack, or a secondary attack if the varg is wielding manufactured weapons.

traits.name: Darkvision
traits.text: Vargs can see perfectly in the dark up to 60 feet.

traits.name: Scent
traits.text: Vargs gain the scent ability.

traits.name: Emotionless
traits.text: Vargs are distrustful and aloof. They do not like dealing with other races other than their own. They receive a –2 penalty on Diplomacy checks when dealing with other races.

traits.name: Size
traits.text: Viera are Medium creatures and thus receive no bonuses or penalties due to their size.

traits.name: Type
traits.text: Viera are Humanoids with the viera subtype.

traits.name: Base Speed
traits.text: Viera have a base speed of 30 feet.

traits.name: Languages
traits.text: Viera begin play speaking Common and Vieran. Viera with high Intelligence scores can choose from the following: Banganese, Elvaan, Lalafellan, Mithran, Moogle, Numish, and Seeq. See the Linguistics skill page for more information about these languages.

traits.name: Vieran Immunities
traits.text: Viera are immune to magic sleep effects and gain a +2 racial saving throw bonus against enfeebling spells and effects.

traits.name: Keen Senses
traits.text: Viera receive a +2 racial bonus on Perception checks.

traits.name: Hunter
traits.text: Viera always count Stealth and Survival as class skills.

traits.name: People of the Wood
traits.text: Viera cling to their fey past, learning all they can of the forest and its ways. Viera gain a +1 racial bonus on Knowledge (nature) and Survival checks.

traits.name: Elemental Summoner
traits.text: Choose one of the following elemental subtypes—earth, fire, ice, lightning, water, wind. When summoning a creature with the chosen subtype with a summon spell, increase the duration of that spell by 2 rounds. This choice is made at character creation, and can only be changed with retraining.

traits.name: Vieran Magic
traits.text: Viera gain a +2 bonus on caster level checks made to overcome spell resistance. In addition, they also receive a +2 racial bonus on Spellcraft checks made to identify the properties of magic items.

traits.name: Weapon Familiarity
traits.text: Viera are proficient with shortbows (including composite shortbows), longbows (including composite longbows), greatbows and orc hornbows.

traits.name: Low-Light Vision
traits.text: Viera can see twice as far as humes in conditions of dim light.

traits.name: Type
traits.text: Amalj’aa are Humanoids with the amal’j’aa subtype.

traits.name: Size
traits.text: Amalj’aa are Medium creatures and thus receive no bonuses or penalties due to their size.

traits.name: Base Speed
traits.text: Amalj’aa have a base speed of 30 feet.

traits.name: Languages
traits.text: Amalj’aa start off with Common and Amalj’aa. Amalj’aa with high Intelligence scores can choose from the following: Celestial, Draconic, Galkan, Goblin, Lalafellan, Mithran, and Orc. See the Linguistics skill page for more information about these languages.

traits.name: Bond to the Land
traits.text: Amalj’aa are quite familiar with desert and sandy lands and gain a +2 dodge bonus to AC when in desert areas.

traits.name: Deathless Spirit
traits.text: Amalj’aa have such a strong will that they tend to resist the effects of negative levels and damage when inflicted. Amalj’aa gain a resistance 5 against shadow damage. They do not lose hit points when they gain a negative level, and they gain a +2 racial bonus on saving throws against death effects, energy drain, negative energy, and spells or spell-like abilities of the necromancy school.

traits.name: Stability
traits.text: Amalj’aa gain a +4 racial bonus to their Combat Maneuver Defense when resisting a bull rush or trip attempt while standing on the ground.

traits.name: Stalker
traits.text: The Amalj’aa have long hunted and preyed upon the weak and such traditions have been passed down. Due to such traditions, the Amalj’aa gain a +2 bonus on all Perception and Survival skill checks and are counted as class skills.

traits.name: Claws
traits.text: Amalj’aa have claw-like fingernails that are stronger then leather and therefore receive two claw attacks, dealing 1d4 damage. These are primary natural attacks.

traits.name: Darkvision
traits.text: Amalj’aa have been known to attack travelers both at night and dusk and therefore receive Darkvision out to 60 feet.

traits.name: Size
traits.text: Anticas are Medium creatures and have no bonuses or penalties due to their size.

traits.name: Type
traits.text: Anticas are Humanoid creatures with the antica subtype.

traits.name: Base Speed
traits.text: Anticas have a base speed of 30 feet and a 15-foot burrowing speed.

traits.name: Languages
traits.text: Anticas begin play understanding (but not speaking) (see limited telepathy) Common and Antican. They can choose from Roegadyn, Galkan, Undercommon, Goblin, and Lamia.

traits.name: This is Nothing
traits.text: Anticas can handle climate change for extreme heat or desert conditions during the day or night.

traits.name: Natural Hunter
traits.text: Anticas receive a +2 racial bonus on Perception, Stealth, and Survival checks.

traits.name: Limited Telepathy
traits.text: Anticas are able to mentally communicate with any creature within 30 feet with whom they share a language.

traits.name: Bite
traits.text: Anticas have such a tremendous bite if you get to close and sometimes can contain certain types of devastating poisons. Anticas gain a natural bite attack, dealing 1d4 points of damage. The bite is a primary attack, or a secondary attack if the creature is wielding manufactured weapons.

traits.name: Claws
traits.text: Anticas have claws for fingers that are stronger then leather (and sometimes even certain metals) and, therefore, receive two claw attacks dealing 1d4 damage. These are primary natural attacks.

traits.name: Relentless
traits.text: When fighting an opponent or a caravan, the anticas will not stop until they have completely overrun and killing their opponent. They gain a +2 bonus on combat maneuver checks made to bull rush or overrun an opponent. This bonus only applies while both the antica and its opponent are standing on the ground.

traits.name: Minesight
traits.text: Anticas burrow deep into the ground, forming massive tunnels that can go on for thousands of miles and have developed darkvision up to 60 feet; however, they are automatically dazzled in bright light and take a –2 penalty on saving throws against spells and effects with the light descriptor.

traits.name: Emotionless
traits.text: Anticas have problems processing emotions properly, and thus take a –4 penalty on Sense Motive checks.

traits.name: Unable to Cast
traits.text: Due to their nature of being mutes, anticas are unable to cast spells normally without either Silent Spell or Telepathic Spellcaster feat.

traits.name: Type
traits.text: Forgiven are outsiders with the native subtype.

traits.name: Size
traits.text: Forgiven are Medium creatures and thus have no bonuses or penalties due to their size.

traits.name: Base Speed
traits.text: Forgiven have a base speed of 30 feet.

traits.name: Languages
traits.text: Forgiven begin play speaking Common and Celestial. Forgiven with high Intelligence scores can choose from the following languages: Draconic, Dwarven, Elven, Mithran, Sylvan and Vieran. See the Linguistics skill page for more information about these languages.

traits.name: Celestial Resistance
traits.text: Forgiven have holy resistance 5, ice resistance 5, and lightning resistance 5.

traits.name: Skill Bonus
traits.text: Forgiven have a +2 racial bonus on Diplomacy and Perception checks.

traits.name: Spell-Like Ability (Sp)
traits.text: Forgiven can use daylight once per day as a spell-like ability (caster level equal to the forgiven’s class level), using their Charisma modifier for spell effects.

traits.name: Darkvision
traits.text: Forgiven have darkvision 60 ft. (they can see perfectly in the dark up to 60 feet.)

traits.name: Size
traits.text: Gnaths are Small creatures and thus gain a +1 size bonus to their AC, a +1 size bonus on attack rolls, a –1 penalty on their combat maneuver checks and to Combat Maneuver Defense, and a +4 size bonus on Stealth checks.

traits.name: Type
traits.text: Gnaths are humanoids with the gnath subtype.

traits.name: Base Speed
traits.text: Gnaths have a base speed of 20 feet and a 20-ft.-burrowing speed.

traits.name: Languages
traits.text: Common and Undercommon. Gnaths with high Intelligence scores can choose from Antican, Goblin, Kobold, and Yagudo.

traits.name: Exoskeleton
traits.text: Gnaths have an exoskeleton that grants them a +1 natural armor bonus.

traits.name: Crafty
traits.text: Gnaths gain a +2 racial bonus on Craft (alchemy) and Profession (miner) checks. Craft (alchemy) is always a class skill for a gnath.

traits.name: Limited Telepathy
traits.text: Gnaths are able to mentally communicate with any creature within 30 feet with whom they share a language.

traits.name: Weapon Familiarity
traits.text: Gnaths are proficient with the scimitar, katana, light and heavy crossbows, and short bows.

traits.name: Carrion Sense
traits.text: Gnaths have a natural ability to sniff out carrion. This functions like the scent ability, but only for corpses and badly wounded creatures (creatures with 25% or fewer hit points).

traits.name: Darkvision
traits.text: Gnaths can see perfectly in the dark up to 60 feet.

traits.name: Light Sensitivity
traits.text: Gnaths mostly live in dark tunnels which have caused them to suffer from light sensitivity.

traits.name: Size
traits.text: Goblins are Small creatures and thus gain a +1 size bonus to their AC, a +1 size bonus on attack rolls, a –1 penalty on their combat maneuver checks and to Combat Maneuver Defense, and a +4 size bonus on Stealth checks.

traits.name: Type
traits.text: Goblins are humanoids with the goblin subtype.

traits.name: Base Speed
traits.text: Goblins are fast for their size and have a base speed of 30 feet.

traits.name: Languages
traits.text: Common and Goblin. Goblins with high Intelligence scores can choose any language they want (except secret languages, such as player-made languages from other campaigns. They can however make their own languages).

traits.name: Craftsman
traits.text: Goblins are very gifted with their hands when creating machines and other things and gain a +2 racial bonus on all Craft or Profession checks to create objects from metal, wood, cloth or stone.

traits.name: Field Medic
traits.text: Having to heal on the fly has given the goblins better aptitude at healing others. Goblins gain a +2 racial bonus on heal checks and count it as a class skill.

traits.name: Goblin’s Unique Handle on Things
traits.text: Goblins are proficient with both short swords and hand axes.

traits.name: Master Tinker
traits.text: Whatever you survive makes you a better tinkerer right? Goblins gain a +1 bonus on Disable Device and Knowledge (engineering) checks. Goblins are also treated as proficient with any non-exotic weapon they have personally crafted.

traits.name: Silver Tongued
traits.text: Unlike moblins or other races, goblins are very talkative and eager to sell wares and set up trades with everyone and gain a +2 bonus on Diplomacy and Bluff checks. In addition, when they use Diplomacy to shift a creature’s attitude, they can do so up to three steps up rather than just two.

traits.name: Thug Life
traits.text: Goblins are adept at taking what isn’t theirs, gaining a +2 racial bonus on the steal combat maneuver.

traits.name: Goblin Punch
traits.text: Once per day, goblins are able to cast Goblin Punch using their Intelligence modifier for the saving throw and their level as the caster level.

traits.name: Low-light Vision
traits.text: A goblin can see twice as far as a hume in starlight, moonlight, torchlight, and similar conditions of poor illumination. He retains the ability to distinguish color and detail under these conditions.

traits.name: Size
traits.text: Ixals are Medium creatures and have no bonuses or penalties due to their size.

traits.name: Type
traits.text: Ixals are humanoids with the ixal subtype.

traits.name: Base Speed
traits.text: Ixals have a base speed of 30 feet.

traits.name: Languages
traits.text: Ixal begin with Common and Yagudo. They can learn any of the beastmen languages. Ixal can learn additional languages by putting ranks into the linguistics skill.

traits.name: Bond to the Ice
traits.text: Ixal are used to the treacherous icy lands of Coerthas or the forested areas of the Black Shroud. Therefore, they gain a +2 dodge bonus to AC in forested or icy terrains. This choice is made at character creation, and cannot be changed.

traits.name: Elemental Resistance
traits.text: Ixal are highly tuned with the wind and gain resistance 5 against wind damage.

traits.name: Craftsman
traits.text: Of those Ixal who do not blindly worship their false god, they are a very crafty race and gain a +2 racial bonus on Craft or Profession checks to create objects from metal, cloth, leather, wood or stone.

traits.name: Craftsman Knowledge
traits.text: Ixal gain Knowledge (technology) and Knowledge (engineering) as class skills. Ixal are also treated as proficient with any non-exotic weapon they have personally crafted.

traits.name: Sky Enthusiasts
traits.text: Ixal gain pilot as a class skill.

traits.name: Elemental Affinity
traits.text: Ixal are treated as 1 level higher when casting spells with the wind descriptor. This ability does not give ixal early access to level-based powers; it only affects powers that they could already use without this ability.

traits.name: Elemental Summoner
traits.text: Choose one of the following elemental subtypes—earth, fire, ice, lightning, water, wind. When summoning a creature with the chosen subtype with a summon spell, increase the duration of that spell by 2 rounds.
